title: incremental-otel-rewrite-and-lightweight-metrics-adapter
creator: Ryan Chen
slo_targets: Upgrade must not increase 95th percentile end-to-end request latency by >5% and memory overhead by >8% under standard simulated load. Trace sampling and metric cardinality must be configurable per-route.
description: Context: Our current tracing and metrics stack mixes a few legacy wrappers around OpenTelemetry and an internal metrics shim. This has caused sporadic CPU spikes and higher memory use in the serving runtime at medium load, and complicates vendor interoperability (exporter switching). Goal: perform an incremental, low-risk migration to a slimmer, opinionated OpenTelemetry client surface and a lightweight metrics adapter that keeps existing dashboards and alerts but reduces allocation churn and dependency surface. Scope: 1) Replace legacy tracer shim with a single, well-tested OTEL wrapper that exposes the same span attributes we depend on; 2) Introduce a metrics adapter that batches counters and gauges and reduces label cardinality by normalizing route tags; 3) Remove deprecated logging hooks that duplicate trace context; 4) Provide a toggleable compatibility layer for a 4-week canary rollout. Non-goals: full rework of dashboards or changing telemetry semantics beyond normalization. Migration plan: - Phase A (canary): deploy OTEL wrapper behind feature flag on subset of API routes (10%) with full exporter telemetry to a staging Grafana/Tempo instance. - Phase B (validate): run side-by-side comparison of traces/metrics for 2 weeks, collect perf profiles, and validate alerts. - Phase C (rollout): enable adapter globally with fallback to legacy shim for 48 hours if regressions detected. Rollback plan: feature flag off + quick restore of legacy shim build (we keep both artifacts in the deployment image). Metrics to track: trace coverage, trace export error rate, p50/p95/p99 request latency, process RSS, GC churn, and allocations/sample. Success criteria: - No more than 5% increase in p95 latency, max 8% memory overhead. - Trace export error rate remains <= 0.1%. - Dashboards show consistent metric names; no alerts fired due to missing metrics. Implementation notes: - Use upstream OpenTelemetry v1.22 (locks in stable exporter APIs) and vendor a small compatibility shim for our existing span attribute names. - Implement batching with adaptive flush intervals to minimize tail latency impact. - Keep the metrics adapter as a small, dependency-free package (no new big libs). - Add unit and integration tests that assert span attribute presence and metric normalization. Artifacts: design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1obs-otel-rewrite (internal); initial benchmark results: https://drive.redwood.company/benchmarks/otel-adapter; PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4521 (initial wrapper), https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/3098 (metrics adapter).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Feature-flagged rollout completed with telemetry validated in staging; 2) No critical alerts triggered after 72h global enablement; 3) Benchmarks show allocations reduced by >=15% on hot paths and p95 latency within target; 4) Code reviewed and merged; 5) Confluence design updated with migration notes and rollback steps.
comments: 2026-02-11 — Kickoff meeting: agreed incremental approach and canary percent (10%). Action: Aisha to produce initial traffic-split plan.
2026-02-18 — Benchmarks: initial microbench shows allocations down ~12% with OTEL wrapper in isolation. Work remains to integrate adaptive batching.
2026-02-27 — PR opened: infra#4521 adds OTEL wrapper behind FF. Requested changes: add more unit tests for span attribute mapping (requested by Mateo).
2026-03-03 — Integration test: metrics adapter integration test failing intermittently under high concurrency — found a race in the batch flush path; hotfix branch created (serving#3098-hotfix).
2026-03-10 — Canary started: 10% traffic to wrapper routes. Early telemetry: trace export error rate 0.06%, p95 +1.8%. Observability team asked for a 24h extended canary to gather more samples.
2026-03-12 — Post-canary sync: decision to widen canary to 25% for edge routes; additional telemetry gating added to the FF so we can auto-roll back on export errors >0.2%.
2026-03-12 — Next steps: finish race fix, add e2e tests for batch flush under concurrency, and schedule final rollout for 2026-03-18 if metrics remain stable.
